title: The auditory striatum in sensory gating and perceptual decision-making
title_zh: 听觉纹状体在感官门控与知觉决策中的作用
abstract: The auditory striatum, a caudal sensory-related region of the basal ganglia, has emerged as an important node linking auditory processing to behavioral responses. It integrates bottom-up auditory information conveyed by thalamic and cortical pathways, while top-down cortical signals and neuromodulatory dopamine inputs dynamically shape this integration, positioning the auditory striatum as a flexible interface between sensory processing and action. Recent circuit-level studies suggest that this region contributes to auditory information filtering, temporal processing, and auditory-guided decision-making through the integration of sensory evidence and local inhibitory mechanisms. These findings provide a circuit framework for understanding how auditory signals are transformed into decision-related representations that can guide behavior. Increasing evidence further suggests that disruption of these weighting and selection processes may contribute to auditory disorders such as tinnitus. Thus, the auditory striatum may represent an important circuit component linking auditory processing, cognitive and neuromodulatory control, and maladaptive auditory behavior.
abstract_zh: 听觉纹状体是基底节后部与感官相关的区域，已成为连接听觉处理与行为反应的重要节点。它整合由丘脑和皮层通路传递的自下而上的听觉信息，同时顶层皮层信号和神经调节性多巴胺输入动态塑造这一整合过程，使听觉纹状体成为感官处理与行动之间的灵活接口。最近的电路层面研究表明，该区域通过整合感官证据和局部抑制机制，参与听觉信息过滤、时间处理和听觉引导的决策制定。这些发现为理解听觉信号如何转化为可指导行为的决策相关表征提供了电路框架。越来越多的证据进一步提示，这些加权与选择过程的失调可能导致听觉障碍，如耳鸣。因此，听觉纹状体可能是连接听觉处理、认知与神经调节控制以及不适应性听觉行为的重要电路成分。
